obtained.how: open-access PDF from the publisher (Copernicus, CC BY 4.0)

claims.claim: at Rotsee, Switzerland, thermal siphons ran on 37 % of days
claims.source_value: 85 of the 227 days with continuous measurements (March 2019–February 2020)
claims.quote: over which 85 d (37 %) were reported as TS events
claims.conditions: days with mooring data at the 4.2-m TS mooring, not all 365 days; none before 28 July, ~50 % in August, 87 % in November, 38 % in December, none later that (warm) winter
claims.note: say "37 % of the 227 days measured"; the abstract's own summary is "more than 50 % of the days from late summer to winter"

claims.claim: the siphons flushed a 1-m-deep plateau in about 10 h
claims.source_value: flushing timescale τF ≈ 9.7 ± 2.7 h for the littoral region upslope of the 4.2-m mooring (length 295 m, mean depth 1.7 m), which contains the ~1-m-deep, 173-m plateau; ~7 h in summer, ~20 h in winter
claims.quote: a flushing timescale of τF ≈ 9.7 ± 2.7 h
claims.conditions: Rotsee (small, wind-sheltered, elongated); unit-width volume V_lit ≈ 499 m²; τF = V_lit/q_avg
claims.note: the region flushed is the 1.7-m-average littoral zone, not the 1-m plateau alone

claims.claim: the same scaling gives about 5.5 h for a Hot Brook cove (project estimate)
claims.source_value: the scaling is τF = Vlit/qavg ≈ 2.99·Llit/(B0·LML)^1/3 (R² = 0.18; 95 % CI of the coefficient 2.83–3.15)
claims.conditions: fitted to Rotsee's TS events; B0 the surface buoyancy flux, LML the length of the mixed region
claims.note: only the scaling is the source's; the 5.5-h Hot Brook figure is project arithmetic and was not rechecked here. The fit is weak (R² 0.18)

claims.claim: a night thermal siphon down the slopes at 0.9 cm/s on calm nights (code: ~0.9 cm/s, peaks 2.6, with a surface return)
claims.source_value: daily average cross-shore velocity 0.9 ± 0.2 cm/s; daily maximum 2.6 ± 0.7 cm/s, in the morning; a surface reverse flow returns pelagic water to the littoral
claims.location: p. 340 (PDF p. 10), §3.4; return flow p. 332 (PDF p. 2)
claims.quote: The daily average velocity Uavg ≈ 0.9 ± 0.2 cm s−1
claims.conditions: TS days at Rotsee, depth-averaged over the bottom 3 m at the 4.2-m mooring; events counted only with weak wind (|L_MO|/h_ML < 0.5) and U > 0.5 cm/s for ≥ 2 h
claims.note: the flow peaks in the morning, after the night's cooling phase, so "night" is approximate

claims.claim: the wind stops the siphon above ~5 m/s
claims.note: Doda et al. give no wind-speed threshold; they classify days by a stability ratio (|L_MO|/h_ML < 0.5 = weak wind) and report that wind events from September to December either suppressed the offshore flow or replaced it with wind-driven circulation (p. 344). The 5 m/s is the project's

notes: Useful values for the rewrite: Rotsee plateau 173 m long, 1 m deep; littoral region 295 m, mean depth 1.7 m, mooring at 4.2 m (Table 1); TS thickness ~1.8 ± 0.2 m; unit-width discharge 0.015 ± 0.004 m²/s; TSs absent before late July because the mixed layer stayed shallower than the mooring depth (stratified flows instead). Rotsee is notably wind-sheltered (a rowing venue), so transfer to Hot Brook's more exposed basins is an assumption.
